title: Luminar Technologies Competitive Position in Autonomous Vehicle Lidar Market
decision_context: Keystone Group is advising a growth equity fund considering a $200M position in Luminar Technologies (LAZR). The fund needs to determine whether Luminar's technology lead in 1550nm lidar is sustainable through 2028 given Tesla's camera-only approach, Mobileye's imaging radar alternative, and multiple Chinese lidar competitors entering at 40-60% lower price points. The investment committee meets in 3 weeks.
surprising_finding: Evidence that Luminar's technology moat is either significantly wider than consensus (e.g., 1550nm wavelength advantages are structurally unreplicable) or significantly narrower (e.g., Chinese competitors have already closed the gap and OEM switching costs are lower than assumed).
day_1_hypothesis: Luminar's 1550nm lidar technology lead is sustainable through 2028 due to manufacturing complexity barriers and existing OEM design wins, but the addressable market is smaller than management guidance suggests because camera-only approaches will capture the L2+/L3 segment.
alternative_hypothesis: Luminar's technology lead erodes by 2027 as Chinese competitors achieve manufacturing scale on comparable 1550nm systems, and the company's path to profitability depends on L4+ adoption timelines that are 3-5 years behind current projections.
